lean.fidelity_note: Products and inverses retain polynomial derivative growth, with constants chosen uniformly before the parent parameter and coefficient fields. The formal statement also permits bounded bilinear products and invertible elements of complete real normed algebras. The consequential difference is that its exponents are nonnegative integers, while part (c) keeps the paper’s specified real exponent $C$. Rounding upward changes the radius condition to $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-\lceil C\rceil}$ and the powers to $\mathsf D^{\lceil C\rceil}$ and $\mathsf D^{2\lceil C\rceil}$. For example, with $C=1/2$ and $\mathsf D=4$, the paper allows $\ell_*=1/2$, whereas the rounded condition requires $\ell_*\le1/4$. Rounding is sufficient when the absolute exponent and radius remain freely adjustable in the construction, but it does not reproduce the literal fixed-exponent clause.
